question: In 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sanga, the Rajput ruler of Mewar in the Battle of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khanwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Khanwa was fought on **March 16, 1527**, between the Mughal Emperor Babur and Rana Sanga, the Rajput ruler of Mewar.
 
• Babur’s victory at Khanwa marked the **consolidation of Mughal power in India**, following his earlier victory in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
 
• Babur employed advanced military tactics, including the use of **field artillery**, which played a decisive role in securing his victory.
 
• The battle ended Rana Sanga’s aspirations of uniting Indian rulers to oppose the Mughal invasion, significantly weakening Rajput resistance.
 
• Khanwa is located in modern-day Rajasthan and is historically significant as one of the pivotal battles in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur’s Military Tactics**

 
 
• Babur introduced the **Ottoman-style Tulughma and Araba tactics** in Indian warfare, which involved splitting the army into smaller units for flexible maneuvers.
 
• He effectively used **gunpowder and artillery** in battles, which was relatively new in Indian warfare at the time.
 
 
 
• **Rana Sanga**
 
 
• Rana Sanga was a prominent Rajput ruler and is remembered for his efforts to resist foreign invasions and unite Indian rulers against Babur.
 
• Despite his defeat at Khanwa, Rana Sanga remains a symbol of Rajput valor and resistance.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Battle**
 
 
• The Battle of Khanwa solidified Babur’s position as the ruler of Northern India and laid the foundation for the Mughal Empire.
 
• It demonstrated the superiority of Babur’s military strategies and modern weaponry over traditional Indian warfare methods.
 
 
 
• **Baburnama**
 
 
• The Battle of Khanwa is vividly described in Babur’s autobiography, **Baburnama**, providing firsthand insight into his strategies and the significance of the victory.
 
• Baburnama remains one of the most important historical sources for the study of Mughal history.
